implementation_summary: safeGet gains allowPrivate (lookup once per hop, pinned, every hop re-checked; only the public-address rule is lifted) and redirectAsResponse; caller headers other than Accept/Accept-Language/User-Agent are dropped on a cross-origin redirect hop. New makeOutboundFetch(opts) returns the checkers' FetchFn: GET only, body cap (over-cap returns status with empty body), timeout, extra headers, redirect limit (a 3xx at the limit is returned with its Location). allowPrivate = opts.allowPrivate !== false && getBrowserPolicy() === null, evaluated per call; it can narrow but never widen and is never taken from the URL. New sameSiteUrl(url, site). Spider sitemap seeding uses the injectable CrawlOptions.outboundFetch (default makeOutboundFetch with customHeaders and a 10 MB cap); Sitemap: lines and <loc>s naming another host are logged via debugLog('crawl') and skipped. RobotsPolicy.fetch(origin, ua, fetchFn = makeOutboundFetch({ allowPrivate: false })): same call signature for callers, missing/refused/unreachable still allows all. contextFetcher(context, deps?) sends context.cookies(url) as a Cookie header through makeOutboundFetch with maxRedirects 0 and returns undefined on refusal/failure.

Spider sitemap/robots fetches no longer carry browser-context cookies (customHeaders are still sent); a sitemap that is only served to signed-in users will no longer seed.
A body over the cap returns an empty body: robots.txt over 512 KB becomes allow-all; an access-check page over 2 MB is judged on status only.
contextFetcher sends only the context's cookies, not other headers the browser context had set; refused or failed requests now return undefined instead of throwing (caller already catches).
safe-net.ts now imports ./browser.js (playwright) and type-only @qa/checkers; no import cycle, tsc clean.
safeGet now drops caller headers other than Accept/Accept-Language/User-Agent on a cross-origin redirect hop (applies to the docs-fetch caller too, which sends only Accept).

RobotsPolicy.fetch and contextFetcher callers need no change. ADR 0031 still lists RobotsPolicy.fetch as 'Not covered'; that line is now stale and the docs owner should update it.
